title: Mirror Mage
summary: Break rune barriers with exactly the right mana, using the properties of definite integrals: splitting, mirroring and symmetry.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 7.10, Some Properties of Definite Integrals
concepts: Splitting an integral where |x − c| changes sign
Adding the mirrored integral: 2I = ∫₀^a [f(x) + f(a − x)] dx
∫₀^2a f(x) dx = 2∫₀^a f(x) dx when f(2a − x) = f(x)
Odd functions over symmetric limits give 0
learningOutcome: The student can evaluate definite integrals with their properties: split at a corner, replace x by a − x and add, use symmetry over [0, 2a] or [−a, a], and crack log integrals.

levels.title: Split at the corner
levels.adds: Baseline: split ∫|x − c| dx at x = c, where the sign changes, and add the two pieces (Ex 7.10 Q5, Q6, Q18).
hints: |x − c| is c − x to the left of c and x − c to the right.
Each piece of |x − c| is a triangle: half base times height.
For |x² − 1|, split at x = 1 (and at −1 if the interval reaches it).

levels.title: Mirror pairs
levels.adds: New: ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a − x) dx; when f(x) + f(a − x) = 1, adding the two gives 2I = a (Ex 7.10 Q1 to Q4, Q17).
hints: Call the integral I and write it again with a − x in place of x.
Add the two forms of I: the integrand often becomes 1.

levels.title: Mirror the power
levels.adds: New: replacing x by 1 − x turns ∫₀¹ x(1 − x)ⁿ dx into ∫₀¹ (1 − x)xⁿ dx, which is easy (Ex 7.10 Q7).
hints: Combine into one fraction 1/m and set m.

levels.title: Full turns
levels.adds: New: ∫₀^2a f = 2∫₀^a f if f(2a − x) = f(x), and 0 if f(2a − x) = −f(x); odd functions vanish (Ex 7.10 Q11, Q13, Q14).
hints: Check whether f(2a − x) is f(x) or −f(x).
Over [−a, a], an odd integrand gives 0 and an even one gives twice ∫₀^a.
sin² x and cos² x average 1/2 over any whole number of half turns.

levels.title: Log runes
levels.adds: New: King’s trick on logs: ∫₀^(π/4) log(1 + tan x) dx = (π/8) log 2, and log sin x over [0, π/2] (Ex 7.10 Q8, Q10, Q16).
hints: Replace x by a − x; for tan, (1 + tan(π/4 − x)) = 2/(1 + tan x).
Add the two forms: the logs combine into log 2.
For log sin x on [0, π/2], use log sin 2x = log 2 + log sin x + log cos x.

misconceptions: Replacing x by a − x changes the value of the integral
An integral of a positive-looking curve cannot be simplified by symmetry
